claims.text: Pack aluminization of refractory high-entropy alloys will improve high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Pack aluminization diffuses aluminum into the alloy surface.
Pack aluminization promotes in situ formation of an Al2O3 layer.
The treatment produces a continuous alumina scale at the alloy surface.
The alumina scale produced by the treatment is adherent.
Aluminization raises the surface aluminum concentration sufficiently for alumina to form during high-temperature exposure.
The alumina formed under the proposed conditions is thermodynamically stable.
The alumina scale acts as a diffusion barrier.
The alumina diffusion barrier slows oxygen ingress and oxidation of the underlying alloy.
After 100 hours at 1000°C in air, the aluminized alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy.
After 100 hours at 1000°C in air, the aluminized alloy will have a thinner oxide layer than the untreated alloy.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys exposed at 1000°C in air for 100 hours typically form a thicker, less protective oxide scale.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys exposed at 1000°C in air for 100 hours typically exhibit higher oxidation weight gain.
The beneficial effect requires enough surface aluminum to form a continuous alumina scale.
The beneficial effect depends on aluminum diffusion kinetics and oxide-scale adhesion.
The magnitude of the oxidation improvement depends on pack-aluminization processing parameters and alloy composition.
